intent: Hold content beside the title, such as a badge, a status, section navigation or a small action.
typical_uses: A badge with the type or state of the object the page shows
A status with a short summary of the object
Navigation between the sections of the page

dont_use_when.situation: The actions the page is worked with

invariants.text: PageHeaderMeta is a flex row that centers its children vertically and spaces them var(--space-5) apart, var(--space-5) after the title. It is as wide as its content; when the row runs short it shares the row with the title, keeping its width while it is narrower than its share, so it does not paint over the actions.
When the header's width inside its side insets is below 64rem it moves under the description, onto a line of its own.

anti_patterns.dont: Use Tabs here for links that open other pages
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use a nav of links with aria-current="page" on the current one; Tabs belong here only when they switch panels on the same page

anti_patterns.dont: Put a sentence about the page beside the title
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put it under the title, in PageHeaderDescription

good.title: A badge beside a project's name
A tab list beside the title, inside the Tabs that also holds the panels it switches
good.code:
<Tabs defaultValue="summary">
  <PageHeader>
    <PageHeaderContent>
      <PageHeaderTitle render={<h2 />}>Overview</PageHeaderTitle>
      <PageHeaderMeta>
        <TabsList variant="line" aria-label="Overview sections">
          <TabsTrigger value="summary">Summary</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="delivery">Delivery</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
      </PageHeaderMeta>
    </PageHeaderContent>
  </PageHeader>
  <TabsContent value="summary">Summary panel</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="delivery">Delivery panel</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

bad.title: A sentence set beside the title
bad.code: <PageHeaderMeta>Every invoice sent to this customer, newest first.</PageHeaderMeta>
bad.why: Beside the title the sentence competes with it for one row and is squeezed to its share of it; under the title, in PageHeaderDescription, it keeps the whole width of the block.
